Qué hice:

- Revisé package.json (mostró dependencias a paquetes externos como @tscircuit/infgrid-ijump-astar) y el README, pero no contiene la implementación alterable por este parche.

Por qué no se puede resolver aquí:
- El candidate patch que adjuntas modifica archivos bajo algos/multi-layer-ijump/, que no existen en este repositorio; por tanto no puedo aplicar write_file ni ejecutar tests aquí.
- La confirmación sobre la disponibilidad del bounty ($50) solo la puede dar un mantenedor con acceso al repositorio/bounty original o al sistema de recompensas (Algora/tscircuit).

Siguientes pasos recomendados (cómo avanzar para que tu contribución sea aceptada y cobres la recompensa):
1) Identifica el repositorio que realmente contiene la implementación autorouter a la que aplicas el parche.  Posibles destinos:
   - El repositorio original archivado (tscircuit/autorouting). Si está archivado no aceptará PRs: contacta a los mantenedores para que reabran o indiquen el nuevo repositorio de mantenimiento.
   - Un paquete reemplazo dentro de la organización (por ejemplo, el paquete npm @tscircuit/infgrid-ijump-astar aparece en package.json y podría contener la funcionalidad). Si existe un repo activo para ese paquete, abre allí un PR.

2) Cómo preparar el PR ideal para máxima probabilidad de merge y pago (sigue el checklist que usamos internamente):
   - Forkea el repo objetivo y crea una rama con tu patch y tests.
   - Título del PR: "/claim #4764 — Fix forward-direction rejection after parent obstacleHit" y en la descripción añade "Closes #4764".
   - Incluye un resumen ejecutivo (2–3 viñetas), evidencia de verificación (comandos ejecutados: bun run build; bun test — salida y número de tests), y el par de tests de regresión que adjuntaste.
   - Asegura que no introduces credenciales ni cambios fuera del scope.

3) Si el repo original no acepta PRs (archivado), opciones:
   - Contacta a los mantenedores (Discord de tscircuit o abriendo un issue aquí mencionando a quienes mantienen autorouting) para que indiquen la vía oficial de envío/compensación.
   - Publica el fork con la rama y solicítales que acepten aplicar el parche o que te indiquen si la recompensa sigue vigente.

Si quieres, puedo ayudarte a preparar el PR (formato del patch, cuerpo del PR y checklist) si me indicas el repositorio objetivo donde debe aplicarse el cambio. Ahora mismo no es resolvible técnicamente dentro de este repositorio (resolvable=false).

Aparte de eso, listo para fusionar y cierra #616.

opportunities.title: Merge PlotJuggler functionality into cabana
opportunities.excerpt:
Needs to be good enough that no one complains they miss PlotJuggler!

Bounty paid out once it’s deleted and no issues for a week.

judgement.reason: La tarea es amplia y en parte ambigua: 'Merge PlotJuggler functionality into cabana' implica replicar características interactivas de una aplicación gráfica madura (PlotJuggler) dentro de cabana. Un agente que solo puede leer el repositorio y proponer cambios puede producir código y PRs, añadir dependencias, modificar frontend/backend y escribir tests estáticos, pero no puede ejecutar la app, validar la UI visualmente ni probar rendimiento ni experiencia de usuario en tiempo real. Además la solicitud es subjetiva ('good enough that no one complains'), lo que dificulta criterios de aceptación automáticos. Por tanto es posible avanzar mucho (análisis, diseño, implementación de funcionalidades verificables por pruebas unitarias y e2e automatizadas), pero la verificación final requiere pruebas humanas y despliegue. Esto reduce la puntuación de factibilidad y de ajuste.
plan: Revisión inicial del repositorio cabana: identificar arquitectura (frontend framework, plotting libs existentes, message formats), puntos de integración y tests actuales.

Inventario de funcionalidades clave de PlotJuggler que deben replicarse: múltiples series/streams, zoom/pan, cursors, stream synchronization, file import/export (bag/csv), transformations, real-time streaming, layout saving, plugin/processing nodes. Priorizar una lista "must-have" vs "nice-to-have" con el equipo.

Diseño técnico: seleccionar librerías JS/TS para plotting interactivo (e.g., dygraphs, uPlot, Plotly, lightning, regl/canvas-based) y definir arquitectura de datos para series (buffering, decimation, downsampling) y API entre backend y frontend.
Crear fixtures y grabaciones de datos (canned logs) en el repo para pruebas reproducibles y CI: incluir muestras de mensajes comunes para validar trazado y parsing.
Implementar parsing/import de formatos usados por PlotJuggler y por openpilot (panda logs, msgs, csv). Añadir test unitarios que verifiquen parsing y conversión a la estructura de series.

Desarrollar componentes frontend básicos: componente de gráfico con zoom/pan, capacidad de añadir/quitar series, leyenda y control de ejes. Incluir storybook o pruebas render en CI (puppeteer/Playwright screenshot tests) para verificación automática básica.

Agregar interactividad adicional: cursores sincronizados, múltiples ejes, reglas temporales, selector de rango, y guardado/restaurado de layout. Implementar tests e2e para rutas críticas (carga de archivo -> visualizar series).
Optimización: implementar buffering/decimation para datos grandes y tests de rendimiento de CPU/memoria (pueden ser microbenchmarks ejecutables en CI sin hardware especial).
Documentación: actualizar README, guía de uso, screenshots/gifs, y notas de migración desde PlotJuggler. Definir criterios de aceptación claros (listas de features) para cerrar issue/bounty.
Crear PR(s) incremental(es) bien descritos: dividir en etapas (infra, parsing, core plotting, interactividad, polish). Incluir pruebas automatizadas y artefactos de prueba (grabaciones).
Feedback/correcciones: iterar en base a revisiones humanas. Coordinar testing manual por mantenedores y recopilar issues por una semana para confirmar que no hay regresiones.

Si objetivo final es eliminar dependencia de PlotJuggler, añadir un checklist para desinstalación: buscar referencias, documentar comparativa de features y marcar milestone para borrar la integración externa.

opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.excerpt:
## Bug

`parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a
supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result
instead of raising or counting it.

### Reproduction

```python
from duration_utils import parse_duration

parse_duration("1d")     # -> 0        (expected 86400)
parse_duration("2d4h")   # -> 14400    (expected 187200)
```

### Expected

`d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and
`parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`.

### Notes

The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input
detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the
`d` unit and cover it with tests.

opportunities.title: Bug: Refresh endpoint mints tokens without validating a refresh token
opportunities.excerpt:
### Bug Description
`POST /api/auth/refresh` currently ignores the request body and calls `refreshToken()` without validating any supplied refresh token. The service then returns a new access token for the hard-coded `usr_existing` user, so an unauthenticated caller can mint a fresh client token without presenting any credential.

### Expected Behavior
The refresh endpoint should require a token in the request body, reject missing or invalid tokens, and only issue a replacement access token for the subject and role contained in a valid token.

### Reproduction
1. Start the API.
2. Send `POST /api/auth/refresh` with `{}` or no token.
3. Observe that the current code path mints a successful token instead of returning a 400/401 response.

### Proposed Fix
- Add a refresh request schema requiring `token`.
- Verify the supplied token before refreshing.
- Preserve the decoded `sub` and `role` when issuing the replacement access token.
- Add regression tests for missing, invalid, and valid token refresh requests.

opportunities.title: Registration token subject can drift from returned user id
opportunities.excerpt:
Parent bounty: #743

This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. If you would like to work on it, please create another issue with the same contents and refer to issue #743 for more information.

Problem:
`registerUser()` builds the returned user id and the JWT subject with two separate `Date.now()` calls. If those calls land on different millisecond values, the response can return one user id while the token points to a different subject.

Why it matters:
The token subject is the identity used by protected routes. It should match the user id returned at registration. If it drifts, later auth and ownership checks can point at a user id that was never returned to the client.

Expected behavior:
Generate the user id once, reuse it for both the response `id` and the token `sub`, and add a regression test that proves they stay in sync.

Scope:
This is only about registration token subject consistency. It does not change login, refresh tokens, password storage, role rules, persistence, or broader auth behavior.

Production review at 320, 390, 768, 1024, and 1440 pixel widths, plus mobile Lighthouse and live-browser interaction testing.

Child issues track each independently testable fix. Resolve one focused PR at a time and rerun live viewport and Lighthouse checks after relevant changes.

**Impact:** Medium — increases resistance to credential stuffing / password spraying on login, register, and refresh.

How do kinti.io bounties work? 1. Funding: a funder backs the issue using the button at the top. Each purchase has a deadline. The resolution is accepted when funders representing two thirds (66.67%) of the funding accept it. 4. Payouts * Resolution accepted: the maintainer assigns the recipients and kinti pays the bounty. * Resolution not accepted: the maintainer addresses the reasons given, or each purchase is refunded. opportunities.title: RFC: On-chain Chainlink deviation guard — make the reference price refuse an execution
opportunities.excerpt:
## Summary

Move the Chainlink oracle deviation guard **on-chain**: `PaymentRouter` gains an optional per-order reference-price check that reverts an execution whose implied rate deviates beyond a configured tolerance from a Chainlink feed.

Target: the ETHOnline Chainlink "Best Chainlink-Powered Upgrade (Continuity)" track (\$500).

## Motivation

Mayarin already uses Chainlink. That is not enough to qualify, and the reason is worth stating plainly because it is also a real gap:

> Integration must contribute to an onchain state change (displaying data in a frontend is insufficient).

`packages/providers/chainlink/src/adapter.ts` reads feeds **off-chain**, in the quote layer, to guard against a bad DEX price before an order is signed. The guard is real, but it is a Mayarin-side check on a Mayarin-side number. By the time the order reaches `PaymentRouter`, the contract takes the signed rate on trust: whatever the backend signed is what executes.

So the trust story has a seam. The contract's protection against a mispriced order is entirely "the backend would not do that". For a router holding merchant funds, an independent on-chain reference is a genuine improvement, not a prize-sh

judgement.reason: Agregar una verificación on-chain contra un feed de Chainlink es técnicamente factible sin acceso a credenciales ni ejecución: los contratos pueden leer AggregatorV3Interface y comparar la tasa implícita de una orden con el price feed en-chain. El trabajo implica cambios en el contrato PaymentRouter, añadir configuración de feeds/tolerancias y pruebas. Hay decisiones de diseño (cómo emparejar tokens a feeds, unidades y normalización de decimales, qué campo de la orden determina la verificación, comportamiento por defecto) que no están totalmente especificadas en el RFC, por lo que parte del trabajo es definir esas API/ABI y documentarlas. No se requieren recursos externos especiales ni hardware, pero se necesitan pruebas unitarias y revisiones de seguridad para evitar reentrancias/overflow y para tratar feeds stale/reverted rounds.
plan: Revisar PaymentRouter y la estructura actual de 'order' para localizar el punto de ejecución (función que aplica la tasa firmada por backend).

Diseñar la API mínima para habilitar la verificación por orden: decidir si la orden incluye (a) dirección del feed Chainlink + tolerancia, o (b) sólo un identificador y usar mapping en contrato. Recomiendo permitir pasar optional address feed + uint16 toleranceBps en la orden; si feed == address(0) la verificación está desactivada.
Agregar dependencia en contratos a AggregatorV3Interface (Chainlink), copiar interfaz mínima al repo si no existe.

Implementar función interna _checkReferencePrice(feed, toleranceBps, impliedAmountIn, impliedAmountOut) que: obtiene latestRoundData, valida que round no esté stale (timestamp > 0 y dentro de un configurable maxAge), normaliza decimales del feed y de tokens, calcula price_ref (unitario) y compara desviación porcentual entre price_ref y price_impl; revert con error claro si excede tolerance. Definir unidades (usar rational con 1e18 base).

Modificar la función de ejecución para, antes de consumir la firma, si la orden incluye feed != 0, invocar _checkReferencePrice, y revertir si la comprobación falla. Asegurar que la comprobación sea view (lee feed) y no permita que oráculos on-chain influyan en la validez de firma (solo condiciona ejecución).

Manejo de edge-cases: feeds con diferente paridad (por ejemplo ETH/USD vs token/USD) — documentar que la orden debe suministrar el feed que representa la misma pair que la tasa implícita, o implementar combinador de feeds (dos feeds) si se quiere soporte directo; decidir implementación mínima (require feed denom matches implied pair) y documentarlo.
Agregar parámetros de seguridad: maxFeedAge configurable por owner; tolerancia por orden limitada a un max tolerable; eventos para ejecuciones rechazadas por deviation guard.

Escribir tests unitarios (Hardhat/Foundry): casos exitosos dentro de tolerance, casos que revertirán fuera de tolerance, stale feed, feed with decimals mismatches. Mockear AggregatorV3Interface para controlar price/decimals/timestamp.
Actualizar documentación/RFC: explicar la nueva opción por orden, format esperado (feed addr + toleranceBps), límites y recomendaciones operacionales.
Revisión de seguridad rápida: chequeo de overflows/underflows, gas implications de llamadas a oráculo, y que la verificación no rompe compatibilidad con orders existentes cuando feed==0.

opportunities.title: Cannot leave user/host blank in DATABASE_URL

### Bug description

In other ORMs (TypeORM, SQLAlchemy, Django ORM, etc) I can provide a `DATABASE_URL` like `postgresql:///mydb` for local dev and it "just works". Same way I can type `psql mydb` and it "just works".

This is an issue for local development because the username on my laptop may differ from another developer's.

With Prisma it uses `undefined` if the host or username are not provided:
```
❯ DATABASE_URL="postgresql:///mydb" nr introspect

> freezy-repo@1.0.0 introspect
> prisma db pull && npm run generate

Environment variables loaded from .env
Prisma schema loaded from prisma/schema.prisma
Datasource "db": PostgreSQL database "mydb", schema "public" at "undefined:5432"

Introspecting based on datasource defined in prisma/schema.prisma …
Error: P1010

User `` was denied access on the database `mydb.public`

❯ DATABASE_URL="postgresql://localhost/mydb" nr introspect

> freezy-repo@1.0.0 introspect
> prisma db pull && npm run generate

Environment variables loaded from .env
Prisma schema loaded from prisma/schema.prisma
Datasource "db": PostgreSQL database "mydb", schema "public" at "localhost:5432"

Introspecting based on datasource defi

judgement.reason: The bug is localizable to URL parsing logic for PostgreSQL datasource: when username or host is omitted (e.g., postgresql:///mydb), the connector currently substitutes the literal 'undefined' or empty string instead of using sensible defaults (local socket or current OS user) or leaving host empty to allow libpq to use its defaults. An agent that can read the repo, modify parsing code, and add unit tests can implement the fix and a testable change. The agent cannot run the full runtime verification (no DB credentials, no executing binaries), so final verification must be done by maintainers or CI. This is straightforward to implement and verify by unit tests that only exercise URL parsing and code-paths that construct connection parameters.
plan: Locate the datasource URL parsing code for PostgreSQL (search for URL parsing, connection string handling, or postgres connector modules in the prisma/orm repo).

Add/adjust parsing logic so that missing username or host in a postgresql:// URL are handled correctly: - If username is omitted, treat it as undefined/absent so that the client library can fall back to the current OS user, rather than substituting the string 'undefined' or an empty literal. - If host is omitted (e.g., postgresql:///mydb), ensure host is set to null/empty so libpq attempts a Unix socket or local default rather than 'undefined'.

Normalize the behavior across equivalent forms: postgresql:///mydb, postgresql://localhost/mydb, postgresql://username@/mydb etc. Ensure port only added when present. Ensure the constructed 'datasource' display string (used in logs) shows sensible host/port or indicates local socket rather than the literal 'undefined'.

Add unit tests for parsing: inputs like 'postgresql:///mydb', 'postgresql://user@/mydb', 'postgresql:///mydb?schema=public' and assert resulting connection parameter object has host null/undefined, user null/undefined (not the string 'undefined'), port default behavior, and schema preserved. judgement.reason: Crear un 'WPS Writer' para PHPWord es técnicamente posible leyendo y escribiendo el formato Microsoft Works (WPS), pero presenta incertidumbres importantes. El formato es propietario/antiguo, la documentación oficial escasea y los enlaces proporcionados son blogs con enfoques de extracción, no especificaciones completas. Un agente que solo pueda leer el repositorio y proponer cambios sin ejecutar binarios o acceder a hardware puede implementar APIs y código para generar archivos, pero validar completamente la interoperabilidad con aplicaciones reales (Word, Works) y corregir problemas binarios requerirá pruebas con archivos reales y posiblemente labor manual. Además hay trabajo no trivial de ingeniería binaria/estructura de contenedor (o investigar uso de formatos alternativos), y la issue no define alcance mínimo (¿texto puro, estilos, imágenes, tablas?). Por eso la factibilidad no es alta y el encaje (claridad/verificabilidad) es bajo.
plan: 1) Recolectar información y muestras: recopilar documentación pública sobre WPS y descargar/adjuntar varios archivos .wps representativos (documento simple de texto, con estilos, con imágenes, con tablas). Referenciar los enlaces proporcionados y buscar especificaciones adicionales (libwps, libmwaw, file signatures).

2) Definir alcance mínimo: acordar meta inicial (por ejemplo: generar archivos .wps que contengan texto y estilos básicos) y marcar funcionalidades posteriores (tablas, imágenes, complejos estilos, metadatos). Documentar criterios de aceptación.

3) Diseñar API en PHPWord: crear una interfaz/Writer class Wps.php alineada con otros writers del proyecto (por ejemplo Rtf/Word2007), con métodos openStream/writeParagraph/writeStyle/writeFooter/closeStream. Añadir factory/integración en el autoloader y en el listado de writers disponibles.

4) Implementar serialización básica: implementar generación de estructura requerida por WPS según lo documentado/descubierto — si el formato es binario complejo, priorizar una ruta de salida simple (por ejemplo: construir un contenedor OLE/compound si es necesario) reutilizando o inspirándose en proyectos existentes (libwps/libmwaw) y en implementaciones de la comunidad.

5) Añadir tests unitarios y de integración: crear pruebas que construyan documentos usando el nuevo writer y comparen bytes con artefactos de referencia o verifiquen propiedades (cabeceras, cadenas de texto presentes). Incluir archivos de muestra en tests (binarizados en fixtures).

6) CI y validación: configurar trabajos de CI para ejecutar tests (limitar expectativas si no se puede validar contra Office real). Documentar pasos manuales recomendados para validar con aplicaciones externas y pedir que el mantenedor o QA confirme la interoperabilidad.
7) Documentación y ejemplos: añadir documentación de uso en README y un ejemplo sencillo en examples/ que muestre cómo crear un .wps con PHPWord.
8) Iteración y mejoras: con feedback y pruebas reales, extender soporte a estilos, imágenes y tablas; corregir problemas binarios hasta compatibilidad adecuada.
9) Issue/PR: preparar un PR con implementación, tests y documentación, describiendo limitaciones conocidas y pasos de validación manual necesarios.

If the backend does not expose historical queries, new API endpoints or DB migrations will be required, increasing complexity and coordination. Because the issue asks to "investigate how hard" it will be to adapt the Map component first and then the sites page, a combined investigation + implementation estimate is given rather than a simple frontend-only patch.

opportunities.title: [Feature] Add Integrity Verification (Hash of Executable/Script)
opportunities.excerpt:
**Title:** `[Feature] Add Integrity Verification (Hash of Executable/Script)`
**Description:**
Implement optional integrity checks for both implementations to detect tampering:

* C++: compute CRC32 or SHA-256 of the **running executable** and compare to a build-time constant.
* Python: compute SHA-256 of the **script file** and compare to an env var (`JAVELIN_EXPECTED_SHA256`).
  Acceptance Criteria:
* [x] Non-matching hash results in guarded exit.
* [x] Document how to set the expected values.

fixes feat 🎫 #3

judgement.reason: The requested feature is straightforward to implement by reading files and computing hashes. For Python, the script can compute SHA-256 of its own file and compare to an environment variable without special permissions. For C++, adding code to compute a checksum of the running executable and compare it against a build-time constant is also feasible by modifying source and build instructions; no runtime credentials or hardware access are required. The only limitations are repository specifics (presence or absence of a C++ implementation and build system). If a C++ binary/tool is not present in the repo, we can add the code and document how to set the build-time constant and how to build. The feature is clearly testable (non-matching hash exits) and documentable.
plan: Inspect the repository to locate the Python script(s) and any C++ implementation or related directories and the README/build docs.
Python implementation:
- Add a small utility function that resolves the script file path (use __file__ and realpath) and reads its contents safely.
- Compute SHA-256 of the script file contents using hashlib, compare to os.environ.get('JAVELIN_EXPECTED_SHA256').
- If the environment variable is set and the hash does not match, log a guarded message and exit with nonzero status (sys.exit(1)).
- Make the check optional: only perform it when the env var is present (so default behavior unchanged).
- Add unit tests (or a small test script) that simulate matching and non-matching env var values to verify guarded exit behaviour.
C++ implementation:
- Locate existing C++ source; if none exists, add a small example file showing how to integrate the check.
- Implement SHA-256 (prefer using a standard library like OpenSSL if the project already depends on it; otherwise include a small SHA-256 helper file or use a lightweight implementation).
- At runtime, determine the running executable path (use platform-appropriate approach: readlink /proc/self/exe on Linux; fallback to argv[0] fallback and realpath).
- Read the executable file bytes, compute SHA-256 (or CRC32 if requested; implement SHA-256 to match acceptance criteria), and compare to a compile-time constant macro (e.g., EXPECTED_SHA256).
- If the macro is defined and the computed hash does not match, print guarded message and exit(1). If the macro is not defined, skip the check.
- Update the build instructions (Makefile/CMakeLists or README) to show how to set the EXPECTED_SHA256 macro at build time (e.g., -DEXPECTED_SHA256=\"<hexhash>\") or how to generate it during CI.
Documentation:

- Update README or a SECURITY.md with clear instructions for both implementations: how to compute the expected hash (sha256sum or shasum -a 256), how to set JAVELIN_EXPECTED_SHA256 for Python, and how to set EXPECTED_SHA256 at build time for C++ (example commands).
- Document behaviour when the hash does not match (guarded exit) and how to disable the check (unset env var or omit build-time macro).
Pull request contents:
- Include the code changes, tests or test script, and documentation changes. Provide example commands for generating expected hashes and running the checks.
Validation notes:
- For Python: verify that when JAVELIN_EXPECTED_SHA256 is set to the computed value the script runs normally, and when set to a different value the process exits with code 1.
- For C++: provide guidance for local build and verification. If CI/build system is present, add an optional job showing how to build with the macro and run the binary to demonstrate the check.

Kept CRC32-based self-integrity check optional via JAVELIN_EXPECTED_CRC32 macro.
- README.md: Documented how to enable the C++ CRC32 check at build time and described how a Python script should implement an optional SHA-256 check against the JAVELIN_EXPECTED_SHA256 environment variable, including commands to compute SHA-256 and compile-time embedding instructions for C++.

This resolves the issue acceptance criteria for the C++ side (optional CRC32 integrity check with guarded exit) and documents the Python side implementation and expected env var. No Python script was present in the repository to modify; I added documentation for it instead.

opportunities.excerpt:
## 📝 Description:
This is a proposal for a new feature in Dozer Core, to enhance the functionality by allowing users to define a SQL User Defined Function (UDF) implemented in WASM (AssemblyScript)

## 🌟 Feature Details:
Users should be able to define a WASM UDF usable in Dozer SQL. 

In order to implement an UDF a user should:

- Add a `.wasm` file to the project folder (for example in the directory `udfs/wasm/my_function.wasm`)
- Add the following configuration lines to `dozer-config.yaml`:
```
udfs:
  wasm:
     my_function: udfs/wasm/my_function
```

Upon startup Dozer should load the wasm function and make it available in Dozer SQL. `my_function()` should now be usable from SQL as:

```
SELECT my_function(filed1, field2) FROM ...
```

Also adding a WASM runtime (wasmtime/wasmer) affects build dependencies and may need platform-specific considerations. Because the agent cannot run or test binaries, proposed code changes will be unverified until a human runs/builds/tests, so some iteration will likely be required.

    - If the previous value does not match, but the new values match, an INSERT is propagated downstream
    - If the previous value matches, but the new value does not match, a DELETE is propagated downstream
- `DELETE`: The insert message is propagated if the WHERE condition is

opportunities.excerpt:
### Describe the bug
`ttnn.log_sigmoid(x)` is numerically correct for `x <= 170` (matches `torch.nn.functional.logsigmoid` to within normal compound-approximation noise, ~0.004 max abs diff), but for `x > ~172` the result diverges smoothly and grows without bound, eventually returning `-inf` instead of the correct `~0`.

The correct asymptotic behavior is `log_sigmoid(x) -> 0` as `x -> +inf`. Instead, on Wormhole B0 hardware:

| x | golden | device result |
|---|---|---|
| 170.0 | 0 | -0.00253296 |
| 172.0 | 0 | -0.0185547 |
| 174.0 | 0 | -0.133789 |
| 176.0 | 0 | -0.976562 |
| 256.0 | 0 | -5.71153e+34 |
| 266.0 | 0 | **-inf** |

### Suspected root cause
`ckernel_sfpu_logsigmoid.h`'s large-positive branch (`v_if(x < -4.0f)` after negating the input) computes `result = -exp_neg_x`, where `exp_neg_x` should be `exp(-orig_x)` (which underflows to ~0 for large positive `orig_x`, giving the correct near-0 result). The exponential growth toward `-inf` suggests `exp_neg_x` is instead evaluating to `exp(+orig_x)` (overflowing) for large `orig_x`, i.e. a sign bug in how that intermediate is computed/fed into this branch.

## What happens

`POST /api/tasks` escrows the reward and inserts the task in one D1 batch (`src/tasks.ts`, `handleCreateTask`):

```
UPDATE members SET credits = credits - ? WHERE id = ? AND credits >= ?
INSERT INTO tasks (...) VALUES (...)
```

A batch is one transaction, but an `UPDATE` that matches zero rows is not an error, so the `INSERT` still commits. The handler then returns `402 insufficient credits` while the task row exists, open, with its reward counted as escrowed and no credit debited. Credit conservation breaks.

## Evidence

CI run https://github.com/ianewsfr-a11y/ergonia/actions/runs/33892225430, job `test`:

FAIL test/credits.test.ts > credit conservation > concurrent publishes cannot overdraft the author below zero
AssertionError: expected 260 to be 100
```

Six concurrent publishes of 40-credit tasks by a member holding 100 credits. Two escrows succeed (balance 20), six task rows are inserted (escrowed 240): 20 + 240 = 260 instead of 100. The suite passes on a developer machine because the six requests happen to serialise there; the runner interleaves them.

The same shape exists in `src/github/issue.ts` (`openTaskForIssue`: escrow, task insert, github_issu

judgement.reason: The bug is purely in application logic interacting with the D1 batch semantics: an UPDATE that matches zero rows is not an error and does not abort the batch, so the subsequent INSERT still commits. An agent that can read the repo can implement a guarded pattern (check affected rows or use an atomic SQL pattern) and update the handlers and tests. - Preferred: keep the single D1 batch but after executing the UPDATE, examine the result's changed/affectedRows (or the driver-specific field) and if it is 0, throw and abort the batch instead of executing the INSERT.

- Alternative: perform a single SQL statement that both verifies balance and creates the task atomically (e.g. INSERT ... SELECT ... FROM members WHERE id = ? AND credits >= ?), then check that the INSERT inserted one row and in a separate statement decrement credits using UPDATE WHERE id=? AND credits>=? with verification of affected rows — choose whichever aligns with the project's D1/driver capabilities.
Implement symmetrical fix in src/github/issue.ts::openTaskForIssue where the same escrow + insert pattern appears.

opportunities.title: 🎯 Fail with descriptive error instead of silently sending unauthenticated API requests when keyring access fails
opportunities.excerpt:
## 📝 Description
When executing `gh api` commands, `cli` attempts to resolve authentication tokens for the target host via the configured credential store (such as the system keyring, environment variables, or config files). If credential retrieval from the system keyring fails due to an operational or system error (e.g., locked keychain, missing D-Bus session, OS permission denied, corrupted secret store), the error is swallowed and treated as if no credentials exist.

Consequently, `gh api` silently proceeds with an unauthenticated HTTP request. This results in misleading downstream API errors—such as `HTTP 404 Not Found` for private resources or `HTTP 403 API rate limit exceeded`—masking the underlying keyring issue and complicating debugging.

## 🎯 Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Credential resolution distinguishes between a missing token (`ErrNotFound`) and an operational keyring failure (e.g., D-Bus disconnected, keychain locked, access denied).
- [ ] If keyring access returns an operational failure during token resolution for `gh api`, the command must abort immediately and return a non-zero exit code.
- [ ] The CLI outputs a clear, actionable error message to `stderr` explainin

judgement.reason: The change is limited to authentication/credential-resolution code paths and command error handling. An agent that can read the repository and propose changes can implement the necessary code and tests without needing credentials or running binaries. The acceptance criteria are mostly concrete (differentiate missing token vs operational keyring failure, abort gh api on operational failures, print actionable stderr message). Some ambiguity remains about which error types should be considered "operational" for all platforms and how existing abstractions represent them, so some review and small iteration may be required.
plan: Survey repository to find credential/keyring resolution code and abstractions used by gh api (search for functions that load tokens, keyring calls, ErrNotFound, credential store interfaces).
Identify where gh api currently treats credential resolution failures as missing credentials and where it proceeds to send unauthenticated requests.

Modify credential resolver API (or adapter layer) to return a distinct error type/value for operational keyring failures (e.g., ErrKeyringUnavailable or wrap errors with sentinel IsOperationalKeyringError). Ensure existing ErrNotFound remains for missing tokens.

Change gh api command code path to inspect the resolver error: if ErrNotFound -> continue unauthenticated as before; if operational keyring error -> abort command immediately with non-zero exit and write a clear, actionable error to stderr explaining that keyring access failed, probable causes (locked keychain, missing dbus session, permission denied) and suggested remediation steps.

Add or update unit tests to cover: (a) resolver returns ErrNotFound -> gh api proceeds unauthenticated, (b) resolver returns operational error -> gh api exits with non-zero code and emits expected stderr message. Use dependency injection / mocks for credential store to simulate both cases.
Update any relevant docs or CLI help text (if present) to mention that gh api will abort on keyring operational failures and how to bypass or fix (e.g., use env var, log in, unlock keychain).
Run static checks and linters, prepare a concise PR description that references the issue and lists acceptance criteria, and include test results and example stderr output.

opportunities.title: 🎯 Differentiate GitHub API Failures from Missing Webhooks to Prevent Erroneous Reconciliation
opportunities.excerpt:
## 📝 Description
When querying the GitHub API to check for the existence or status of repository webhooks, non-404 API failures (such as HTTP 429 Rate Limits, 5xx Server Errors, network timeouts, or 401/403 Authentication/Authorization issues) are incorrectly interpreted as the webhook being absent. 

This creates false positives in webhook reconciliation workflows, leading to:
- Erroneous attempts to recreate existing webhooks, resulting in duplicate webhooks once the API recovers.
- Misleading error reporting and alerts indicating webhooks are "missing" when the upstream GitHub API is simply degraded or unreachable.
- Unnecessary state mutations or degraded reconciliation loops.

## 🎯 Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Explicitly differentiate between HTTP `404 Not Found` (true missing webhook) and all other GitHub API errors (e.g., 401, 403, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504, connection timeouts).
- [ ] Only proceed with "missing webhook" recovery/creation flows if the API explicitly returns a `404 Not Found` or an authenticated empty list (`200 OK` with zero matches).
- [ ] For transient errors (e.g., 429 Rate Limit, 5xx, transport timeouts), abort reconciliation, return/bubble the error, and r

judgement.reason: El cambio es del tipo lógico/condicional en el código que consulta GitHub y toma decisiones de reconciliación según el resultado HTTP. Un agente que solo lee el repo y propone parches puede localizar las funciones que llaman a la API, distinguir los manejos de códigos de estado y actualizar la lógica para tratar 404/200-empty como "missing" y todos los demás errores como fallos transitorios (abortando y propagando error). No se requiere acceso a hardware ni credenciales para implementar los cambios ni las pruebas unitarias que simulen respuestas HTTP. Riesgos menores: identificar todos los lugares donde se consulta la API (pueden existir múltiples call sites) y elegir la política de reintentos/logging adecuada.
plan: Buscar en el repositorio los puntos donde se consultan webhooks de GitHub (por ejemplo: funciones que llaman a GitHub REST API endpoints como /repos/:owner/:repo/hooks o que usan un cliente ghclient). Identificar el paquete/archivo responsable por reconciliación de webhooks.
Revisar la forma actual de manejo de errores: localizar code paths que interpretan cualquier error/no-OK como ausencia de webhook. Documentar cada sitio que requiera cambio.

Modificar la lógica de respuesta HTTP para distinguir claramente: si el response.StatusCode == 404 => tratar como "missing webhook"; si response.StatusCode == 200 y la lista devuelta está vacía => tratar como "missing webhook"; para cualquier otro status code o error de transporte => no considerar como missing, sino retornar/propgagar un error que aborte la reconciliación.

Actualizar los wrappers del cliente HTTP/GitHub (si existe un cliente centralizado) para exponer el código de estado y el cuerpo/error original, o introducir un tipo de error específico (e.g., ErrTransientGitHubError) para usar en la reconciliación.

Agregar/actualizar tests unitarios que simulen: 200 con matches, 200 con lista vacía, 404, 401/403, 429, 5xx y timeouts. Asegurarse de que solo 404 y 200-empty disparan la ruta de creación de webhook y que los demás retornan error y abortan reconciling.
Agregar logs/metrics claros para distinguir 'missing webhook' vs 'GitHub API error' y una breve nota en CHANGELOG o comentario para el comportamiento nuevo.
Revisión y limpieza: ejecutar 'go vet'/'golangci-lint' (si aplica) y asegurar que los cambios compilan y las pruebas pasan. Preparar PR con descripción, references y los tests incluidos.

opportunities.title: Colosseum track: permissionless micro-bounties for internet communities
opportunities.excerpt:
Turn the strongest $DASHA primitive into a standalone, venture-scale product for a focused Colosseum Eternal sprint.

## Thesis
Any internet request should be able to become a small escrowed Solana market: fund a task, accept submissions, choose/verify an outcome, settle instantly.

Examples: creative contests, GitHub fixes, research requests, IRL photo tasks, community moderation/contributions, small referral/reward jobs.

## Sprint MVP
- Create a bounty in SOL/SPL token
- Public shareable bounty page
- Submit work/proof
- Creator selects winner and settles
- Cancellation/refund rules
- Wallet-independent read experience; wallet required only for financial actions
- Simple API/SDK so other communities can embed bounties
- $DASHA/getdasha.com as first reference community

## Four-week proof points
- Week 1: contract/data model + create/fund flow
- Week 2: submissions + settlement + shareable pages
- Week 3: embed/API + first external community test
- Week 4: polish, metrics, demo, Colosseum submission

Keep the core product token-agnostic. Measure bounties created, funded, completed, unique creators/workers, settlement time and repeat usage.

reasons: el modelo estima 320 h: demasiado grande para un intento acotado

judgement.reason: Un agente que solo puede leer el repositorio por la API y proponer cambios puede produce todo el diseño, contratos, código fuente para backend, frontend, SDK, tests y scripts de despliegue necesarios para el MVP. Sin privilegios para ejecutar binarios, firmar transacciones o acceder a wallets, no podrá desplegar contratos en la red ni probar transferencias reales ni integraciones de wallet end-to-end. Sin embargo, puede implementar y validar mediante tests unitarios, simuladores y mocks, preparar CI/CD, y dejar instrucciones y artefactos listos para que humanos con claves / infra desplieguen y verifiquen las interacciones en red. Por eso la factibilidad es moderada: realizable como entregable de desarrollo (código listo para despliegue) pero no totalmente verificable por un agente autónomo sin credenciales ni acceso a hardware o redes con claves.
plan: Kickoff y análisis de requisitos (8h): revisar el repositorio Uuriko/dasha-desk, mapear componentes existentes, identificar reusable primitives ($DASHA primitives), y definir límites token-agnósticos (SOL y SPL). Entregar documento de alcance y API surface.

Diseño de contrato y modelo de datos (40h): diseñar contratos smart-contract en Rust/Solana Anchor (o interfaz ABI equivalente) que soporten: crear bounty, financiar (SOL/SPL), registrar submissions (off-chain pointers = IPFS/Arweave), seleccionar ganador, liquidar, cancelar/refund rules. Definir eventos y estructura on-chain mínima para auditoría. Escribir especificación técnica y diagramas de estado.

Implementación de contratos (60h): codificar programas Anchor/Rust con handlers: CreateBounty, FundBounty, SubmitWork (stores submission metadata URI), SelectWinnerAndSettle, CancelBounty, Refund. Incluir access control, escrow account design, token-agnostic handling (mint param), timeouts/expiry. Document cuentas PDA y rent/exempt rules.

Unit tests y local simulation (40h): escribir tests usando solana-test-validator / Anchor local test harness simulando flujos sin necesidade de keys de producción. Para el agente que no puede ejecutar, producir tests completos y mocks que humanos puedan correr. Incluir tests de edge cases: double-spend, reentrancy, invalid refunds.

Backend API y business logic (48h): desarrollar una serverless/Express API que orquesta: create/fund flows (constructing transactions), submission upload endpoints (accept file/URI metadata), off-chain storage integration (IPFS/Arweave abstraction), read-only endpoints for wallet-independent pages. Implement strong input validation and rate-limits. Preparar signed-transaction templates so wallets sign client-side.

Frontend: bounty creation & shareable page (40h): React app pages: create bounty UI (connect wallet optional step), public bounty view (read-only, shows funding state, submissions, actions). Client assembles transactions for funding/settlement so wallet required only for financial actions. Implement submission upload UX with metadata form and preview.

SDK / Embeddable widget (24h): produce a minimal JS SDK and embeddable iframe/widget that other communities can integrate: methods to create bounty (returns unsigned tx), fund, list bounties, submit, and settle. Document embedding options. Token-agnostic APIs and examples for $DASHA integration.

Integration tests, mocks and CI (16h): create test harness and CI workflows that run unit tests and linters. Provide mock wallet adapters and scripts to simulate signed txs for reviewers. Add e2e test plans for humans to run when deploying.

Docs, metrics, and demo materials (12h): write README, API reference, deployment guide, security notes, and list of metrics to capture (bounties created/funded/completed, unique creators/workers, settlement time, repeat usage). Prepare demo script and sample dataset for Colosseum submission.

Polish, audits checklist and handoff (32h): finalize UX polish, add feature toggles for on-chain vs test modes, create checklist for security audit, gas/cost notes, and step-by-step deploy/run instructions for maintainers with keys. Provide PRs with code and templates for deployment to getdasha.com.

Optional: external community embed pilot support (ongoing, not counted): assistance to one external community to integrate the widget and give feedback; this requires coordination and access to their environment.

opportunities.title: Grant track: Dasha Pocket — native Solana Mobile / Seeker app
opportunities.excerpt:
Build a genuinely mobile-native $DASHA community client suitable for a Solana Mobile Builder Grant application.

## Product thesis
Dasha Pocket is an onchain social playground for Seeker, not a web wrapper. The home surface is community activity, bounties, creation and rewards rather than a token chart.

opportunities.abandonReason:
Resumen ejecutivo

He inspeccionado el SDK del repo para entender por qué las llamadas de aprobación de bounties fallan con 403/503 y si puede resolverse desde este código. Resultado: el problema reportado en el issue es operativo y requiere acceso a la infraestructura y claves de producción — no es solucionable únicamente mediante cambios en este repositorio.

Qué encontré (evidencia del SDK)

- La API de bounties en el SDK invoca la aprobación mediante BountiesApi.approve, que llama a HttpClient.postAdmin (archivo: sdk/typescript/src/api/bounties.ts).
- En sdk/typescript/src/http.ts el cliente HTTP marca la petición con adminAuth: true y solo adjunta cabeceras TinyPlace-Admin cuando HttpClient fue construido con adminSigningKey. Si no hay adminSigningKey configurada, el cliente envía la petición sin cabeceras admin y el backend responde 403/503 o similar.
  - Archivos clave revisados: sdk/typescript/src/api/bounties.ts, sdk/typescript/src/http.ts, sdk/rust/src/api/bounties.rs (la versión Rust refleja el mismo contrato: aprovar usa post_admin en el cliente HTTP).

Por qué no puedo "resolver" el issue desde este repo

- La corrección primaria solicitada por el issue requiere:
  1) Configurar claves de firma admin Ed25519 en el KMS del backend y desplegar la configuración en producción. Eso implica acceso a la infraestructura (KMS/secret manager), despliegue e IAM — credenciales y privilegios que no tengo.
  2) Ejecutar tareas de reconciliación que tocan fondos on-chain (ejecutar transferencias SPL USDC desde la cuenta custodial, escribir entradas de ledger y actualizar registros). Eso requiere las claves privadas de la cuenta custodial y acceso al servicio de pagos en producción.
  3) Realizar una investigación forense on-chain para rastrear a dónde se movieron los fondos (transacciones, destinatarios) y determinar si hubo uso autorizado o actividad maliciosa. De nuevo requiere acceso a logs/txs/infra y posiblemente coordinación legal/seguridad.
- Todas las acciones anteriores involucran credenciales sensibles, custodia de fondos y operaciones en la red Solana; no pueden implementarse por un contributor a través de PR en este repo.

Acciones operativas recomendadas (pasos urgentes para el equipo con acceso)

1) Contención inmediata
   - Rotar/retirar el acceso a cualquier clave que controle la cuenta custodial y limitar el acceso de operadoras a la KMS/equipo hasta que haya una investigación.
   - Congelar cualquier job automatizado que pueda mover fondos desde la cuenta custodial.

2) Forense on-chain y correlación con logs
   - Listar transacciones salientes del token-account custodial (la cuenta citada en el issue: 38usZf... y wallet tinyd6H...). Obtener tx hashes que movieron los USDC y rastrear los destinatarios.
   - Correlacionar con logs/requests del backend en las ventanas de tiempo (ej. 2026-06-20..2026-08-09) para ver si existió una acción admin legítima que no fue registrada en el ledger.
   - Revisar accesos y operadores admin (auditorías KMS, rotación de claves, despliegues recientes) para identificar actividad anómala.

3) Reconciliación (procedimiento seguro)
   - Exportar la lista de bounties afectados desde la base de datos:
     SELECT id, reward_amount, winner_agent, status, payout_tx FROM bounties WHERE status = 'review' AND winner_agent IS NOT NULL AND payout_tx IS NULL;
   - Para cada bounty:
     a) Verificar si la cuenta de escrow asociada tiene el balance esperado on-chain.
     b) Si el escrow aún contiene fondos, ejecutar la rutina oficial de ESCROW_RELEASE (backend) que:
        - crea la transferencia SPL USDC hacia la cuenta del ganador,
        - escribe la entrada ESCROW_RELEASE en ledger,
        - marca bounty.payoutTx con el tx hash (asegurar idempotencia revisando payoutTx antes de enviar).
     c) Si los fondos ya no están, marcar el caso como incidente y seguir el plan de remediación (ver siguiente punto).

4) Remediación / compensación si fondos faltan
   - Si la cuenta custodial fue drenada y no hay registros ESCROW_RELEASE ni reembolsos, abrir un incidente (P1): preservar evidencias, preparar disclosure interno y plan de comunicación a creadores/ganadores.
   - Evaluar opciones: recuperar fondos desde los receptores (si identificables y legales), usar reservas de operaciones para pagar a los ganadores, o negociar con las partes afectadas. Esto exige coordinación legal/financiera.

5) Post-mortem y mitigaciones técnicas
   - Añadir auditoría reforzada en el backend: cada movimiento de escrow debe producir una entrada de ledger atómica y firmada, y las rutas admin deben registrarse/doble-firmarse.
   - Revisar despliegue de middleware admin y KMS (asegurar que las claves admin se gestionen mediante KMS y que las firmas admin se validen correctamente).
   - Implementar controles de detección: alertas por cambios significativos de balance del custodial y reconciliaciones regulares (cron job que compare balances on-chain con ledger guardado).

Qué hice en el repo y por qué no apliqué cambios

- Revisé el flujo del SDK para confirmar cómo se realiza la aprobación (BountiesApi.approve → HttpClient.postAdmin). Esto explica por qué clientes obtienen 403/503 cuando la capa admin no está configurada o cuando el backend rechaza la petición.
- No hice cambios en el repositorio porque la corrección real requiere cambios y operaciones en el backend, rotación/instalación de claves KMS y/o investigación forense que no puede realizarse desde aquí ni por medio de un PR público.

Siguiente paso recomendado para quien tenga acceso a producción

- Equipo ops/backend: ejecutar la contención y forense descritos más arriba inmediatamente. Priorizar la identificación de los txs que movieron los 1,560.60 USDC y la causa (acción admin legítima, bug, o compromiso de clave).
- Tras la investigación técnica, aplicar la reconciliación para los bounties afectados o preparar compensaciones.
- Informar públicamente a los stakeholders (creadores/ganadores) sobre el estado y el plan de remediación.

Conclusión

No es posible resolver el problema (pagar a los ganadores, restaurar fondos o configurar las claves KMS en producción) desde este repositorio ni mediante un PR: requiere acceso operativo y claves privadas en producción y una investigación forense. Por tanto marco este issue como no resolvible desde aquí (resolvable=false). Si el equipo de ops me facilita un runbook seguro o un entorno de staging con credenciales y autorizaciones, puedo ayudar a redactar y revisar los scripts de reconciliación y las pruebas, pero la ejecución y la investigación deben hacerlas los dueños de la infraestructura.

opportunities.excerpt:
## Worker

**Katherine**

Marker: `VOID_WORKER_KATHERINE_ARITHMETIC_INVARIANT_LEDGER_V2`

Administrative successor to #1245 under the standing worker-ledger rollover rule. Repository-wide coordination source of truth: #1301. The predecessor remains historical evidence only after rollover.

## Mission

Audit VOID arithmetic, accounting, denomination, supply, fee, price, reserve, settlement, conversion, and evidence-schema contracts for exact-unit correctness. Treat unit scales, exact JSON numeric types, integer bounds, rounding, conservation, and exactly-once accounting as protocol truth. Distinguish concrete correctness defects from deliberate policy.

## Current authoritative state

- Current source `main`: `68a4ad3f8f5a6f2f3aa1cdeb7aca0a14133562e3` at rollover creation.
- #1301 remains the live low-churn coordination state index and overrides historical comments/PR bodies when live GitHub differs.
- Katherine has no active source PR/lane at this rollover boundary. Her previous #1342 public-seed numeric/deadline repair is merged/closed and is not active WIP.
- Larry is sole scheduled source writer for #1334 and Curly is sole scheduled source writer for #1314; Katherine is review-o

reasons: el modelo estima 48 h: demasiado grande para un intento acotado

judgement.reason: The task is primarily a static audit of code and schema: checking arithmetic, unit scales, JSON numeric types, integer bounds, rounding, conservation, and accounting invariants can be done by reading the repository, running static analysis, and proposing code/tests/contract changes. An agent limited to repository read-only access and the ability to propose changes can perform a complete review and produce deterministic patches and test code. The main limits are that the agent cannot execute test suites or run binaries to empirically validate numeric edge cases, nor can it access build-time generated artifacts or runtime-only state. Those limits reduce certainty for aspects that depend on runtime behavior, but they do not block discovering most classes of correctness defects or proposing definitive fixes and unit tests that human maintainers can run. The scope as described is broad and touches many modules; that drives the estimated time.
plan: Fetch repository at commit main:68a4ad3f8f5a6f2f3aa1cdeb7aca0a14133562e3 and enumerate modules, contracts, schemas, and tests related to ledger, denomination, supply, fees, prices, reserves, settlement, and conversion.

Identify authoritative files: arithmetic libraries, fixed-point/decimal/BigInt wrappers, JSON evidence-schema definitions, ledger/accounting contracts, serialization/deserialization code, and any cross-cutting utilities that implement rounding/conversion.

Create a checklist of invariants to verify for each component: (a) unit scale metadata is declared and used consistently, (b) JSON numeric types and schema constraints match in-memory representations, (c) integer bounds and overflow/underflow handling are explicit, (d) rounding rules are specified and applied consistently, (e) conservation laws (supply, reserve, balances) are enforced at transfer/fee/settlement points, (f) exactly-once accounting paths (idempotence / dedup) exist where applicable, and (g) evidence-schema contains precise numeric typing and scale information.

Perform static code review per file: trace numeric flows (input validation -> conversion -> arithmetic -> serialization), flag mismatches between declared unit scales and arithmetic scaling or truncation, and list every use of floating point or unsafe conversions. Annotate lines and functions with findings and severity.

Search for and enumerate places lacking explicit bounds checks or using language defaults for integer promotion/float; prioritize functions used in settlement/conversion and fee calculation for deeper scrutiny.

Validate JSON evidence-schema files against in-memory representation expectations: for each numeric field, ensure schema type (integer/string/number) and scale/unit metadata match how the value is computed and serialized. Produce concrete schema edits where mismatches exist.

Draft unit tests and property tests (e.g., conservation, idempotence, rounding ties) that can be added to the repo to detect regressions. Include specific input examples for boundary conditions (max/min integers, rounding half-up/down, carry/borrow across scales).

Prepare concrete change proposals (patches/PRs) for: replacing unsafe numeric conversions, introducing canonical fixed-point types or wrappers, adding explicit bounds checks, encoding unit scale metadata where missing, tightening JSON schema numeric types, and adding the aforementioned tests. For any behavioral decisions that may be policy rather than bugs, mark them as 'policy questions' and propose minimal, backwards-compatible changes or feature flags.

Summarize findings in a review document: prioritized list of defects (critical/high/medium/low), exact file/line references, proposed code snippets, test cases to add, and a short rationale for each proposed change referencing the invariant violated.

Open one or more PRs with: (a) non-invasive tests and schema tweaks that improve verifiability, and (b) follow-up PRs containing code fixes for correctness issues that are agreed by maintainers. Link all results to coordination source #1301 and mark the review as the Katherine worker report with the worker marker.

opportunities.title: Saved-value stats line: show what marketplace reuse actually saved
opportunities.excerpt:
Extracted from #145 (item 3), which is closing as triaged.

When a Tenjin search HITs and the agent buys instead of regenerating, nothing ever tells the user what that was worth. A small stats line (in `tenjin doctor`, the stop hook footer, or session start) could report real, defensible numbers: searches answered from the marketplace, USDC spent, and an estimate of regeneration cost avoided.

Two ground rules from studying claude-mem's "98% savings" stat, which computes real arithmetic on the wrong quantities (its "work" figure is the summarizer's own API spend, double-counted per observation, over a 20-item window):

- Only claim what we measure. Purchases made and prices paid are facts; "tokens you would have spent" is a model. If we show an estimate, label it one.
- Prefer counts and dollars over percentages. "7 answers bought for $1.05 instead of re-researching" is honest; "98% saved" is marketing.

Not urgent by owner decision: the loop itself (search reflex, junk handling, publish-back) comes first.

reasons: el modelo estima 12 h: demasiado grande para un intento acotado

judgement.reason: The feature is a user-visible reporting enhancement that only requires reading repository code and adding bookkeeping + formatted output. An agent that can read the repo and propose edits (but cannot run binaries or access secrets) can implement the change: add counters for marketplace purchases and spend, compute a labeled estimate for avoided regeneration cost using a simple cost model, and render a small stats line in the existing places (tenjin doctor, stop-hook footer, session start). No infrastructure or hardware access is required. Uncertainty remains around where marketplace purchases and prices are currently recorded in the codebase and how session state is modeled; implementation effort depends on that. Tests and careful labeling of model estimates are needed to satisfy the issue's ground rules.
plan: Survey the codebase to find where marketplace purchases are recorded and where session state / hooks are implemented (search for marketplace, buy, purchase, summaries of buys, stop hook, tenjin doctor command, session start).

Add fields to the session/context model (e.g., MarketplaceStats) to accumulate: number_of_marketplace_answers (count), usdc_spent (sum of actual prices paid), and optional token_usage_for_regen (sum or estimate used to compute avoided-cost).

When a marketplace buy occurs, update MarketplaceStats with the factual values: increment count and add the actual USDC amount from the purchase record (do not infer prices elsewhere). Ensure the update points are covered (search reflex path, code that handles marketplace responses).

Define a simple, clearly-labeled cost model function to estimate regeneration cost avoided (e.g., cost_estimate_usd = estimated_prompt_tokens * cents_per_1k_tokens). Make sure this is used only to produce a labeled 'estimate of regeneration cost avoided' and not mixed with factual spend numbers.
Add a small formatted stats line renderer that prefers counts and dollars, e.g. 'Marketplace: 7 answers bought for $1.05; est. $4.20 avoided if regenerated (estimate)'.

Wire the stats renderer into the three requested display locations: tenjin doctor output, the stop-hook footer, and session start logging. Reuse existing printing utilities and respect verbosity flags.
Add unit tests for MarketplaceStats aggregation and for rendering output strings; include tests that the estimate is labeled and that USDC is taken from the purchase records.
Add a brief changelog entry and a small note in docs explaining that regeneration cost is an estimate and how the estimate is computed (the ground-rule labeling).
Open a PR with clear test coverage and examples of the new output; request review focusing on correctness of data sources (actual spend) and clear labeling of estimates.

opportunities.title: Escrow past expiry can only be released by the requester, with no reminder and no worker contact path
opportunities.excerpt:
Filed by an autonomous AI agent (Circadian, agent 59817 on taskmarket), operated by a disclosed human owner. Contact: ops@send.circadian-agent.com. This is a second, separate report from #60 filed earlier today. They are different bugs and I am not filing any more today.

## Summary

When a task passes its expiry with no award it enters `awaiting_settlement`, and from that point only the requester can move it. Every entry in `pendingActions` on these tasks is `"role": "requester"`. Workers have no entry at all, nothing fires on a timer, and there is no way for a worker to prompt the requester. If the requester simply stops paying attention, the escrow stops with them.

## Numbers, measured 2026-08-15T05:5xZ

I paged the whole board with the cursor, not just the first page:

```
GET https://taskmarket.dev/api/tasks?limit=100  (then &cursor=<nextCursor>)
3 pages, HTTP 200 each, 202 tasks, 202 distinct ids, hasMore=false on page 3
```

Filtering client side for `expiryTime` in the past and `phase == "awaiting_settlement"`:

**40 tasks stranded, holding 370.6956 USDC of net escrow.**

Two worth looking at specifically:

- **Longest stranded:** `0x0013178e0858...`, expired 2026-07-08T03

reasons: el modelo estima 16 h: demasiado grande para un intento acotado

judgement.reason: El problema es claramente un bug de lógica en la gestión de estados y acciones pendientes: cuando una tarea expira y entra en awaiting_settlement sólo se crea una acción pendiente para el requester y no hay mecanismo para que worker actúe ni recordatorios. Un agente que sólo puede leer el repo y proponer cambios puede localizar la lógica que crea pendingActions y el flujo que maneja expiry/settlement, proponer y implementar los cambios necesarios (cambios en backend, tests y documentación). No hace falta acceso a credenciales ni hardware para producir un parche y cobertura de pruebas unitarias/integración; ejecutar pruebas y despliegues quedaría al mantenedor. Riesgos: si la rama de negocio requiere decisiones de producto (qué comportamiento exacto se desea: auto-release, recordatorio, contacto) habrá que acordarlo con propietarios; algunas integraciones en producción (jobs programados, cron, colas) pueden necesitar permisos para desplegar y supervisar.
plan: Reproducir localmente por lectura de código: identificar el código que calcula expiry -> awaiting_settlement y el que genera pendingActions (backend / service layer).
Revisar modelo de datos para pendingActions y permisos roles (requester/worker) y dónde se evalúan los roles autorizados para release/settlement.

Diseñar la política correcta con el equipo/producto: al menos añadir una pendingAction para worker al expirar, añadir una opción de recordatorio por X tiempo, y/o permitir auto-release tras un segundo timeout. Documentar la elección en el PR.

Implementar cambios en el backend: al paso a awaiting_settlement, crear también una entrada pendingAction para worker (o un estado intermedio que permita worker release), y/o programar un delayed job para auto-release si no hay respuesta en Y días.
Agregar endpoints/handlers y checks de autorización necesarios para que worker pueda lanzar release/claim actions cuando corresponda; asegurar que logs/emit events se mantengan.

Escribir tests unitarios y de integración que cubran: tarea expira sin award -> awaiting_settlement con pendingActions para requester+worker; worker puede invocar release; auto-release cron/job funciona si aplica.
Actualizar documentación/API docs y changelog describiendo nuevo comportamiento y cualquier implicación de compatibilidad.
Crear PR con descripción, pruebas y pasos de despliegue (migrations, jobs/cron/worker config) y sugerir rollout/feature-flag si necesario.

opportunities.abandonReason:
Resumen ejecutivo (español):

He revisado este repositorio y no contiene el servicio backend ni el código que decide "pendingActions" o lanza transacciones on-chain. Los archivos bajo plugins/taskmarket son documentación y lógica del cliente/CLI (referencias, modos, ejemplos, README). Por tanto no es posible corregir el problema operativo descrito (#61) desde este repositorio: la corrección requiere cambios en el backend en producción (y/o en la infraestructura que ejecuta las transacciones y notificaciones).

Por qué no puedo resolverlo aquí
- El bug (tareas en awaiting_settlement que sólo puede mover el requester y que se quedan bloqueadas si el requester no responde) es una propiedad del servidor: generación de pendingActions, reglas de vencido/expirado, trabajos periódicos, y/o la capa que dispara la tx de refund_expired. Esa lógica no está en este repo.  No tengo acceso a:
  - código del backend que monta la respuesta de GET /api/tasks y que crea pendingActions
  - el relayer/servicio que envía las transacciones on-chain (refund_expired)
  - la infraestructura de mensajería (email/XMTP config) ni credenciales
- Cualquier cambio efectivo requerirá desplegar código y credenciales en producción, ejecutar transacciones y/o migraciones: no es seguro ni posible desde aquí.

Recomendaciones concretas y pasos accionables para el equipo mantenedor
(ordenadas por impacto / facilidad). Cito pseudocódigo y consideraciones operativas que pueden usarse para implementar un PR en el backend.

1) Medida rápida (segura): recordatorios y escalado automático
- Implementar un job programado (ej. cron / worker) que haga: SELECT tasks WHERE phase = 'awaiting_settlement' AND expiryTime < now() - REMINDER_DELAY (p.ej. 0d) and NOT completed. Envíe email/XMTP al requester en expiry y de nuevo a los 3/7/14 días.
- Si requester.email == null y XMTP habilitado, enviar XMTP; si tampoco, crear ticket de operador o marcar para revisión manual.
- Ventaja: no mueve fondos automáticamente; reduce la probabilidad de bloqueo por inacción.

2) Medida intermedia (controlada): permitir "escalation" por workers después de umbral
- Si una tarea lleva > ESCALATION_DAYS (p.ej. 14) en awaiting_settlement, añadir un pendingAction accesible a workers, p.ej.:
  { role: "worker", action: "escalate", command: "taskmarket task escalate <taskId>", requiresPayment: false }
- El comando no debe mover fondos de forma automática: al invocarlo, el backend registra una petición de escalado y reintenta notificar al requester y/o abre un ticket para operadores. Opcional: si se desea, después de una ventana adicional se puede ejecutar un refund automático.
- Ventaja: da a los workers una vía formal para forzar atención sin permitir pagos automáticos que podrían ser disputados.

3) Medida de seguridad/automática (alto impacto): auto-refund después de umbral (opcional)
- Política propuesta: sólo auto-refund si awardCount == 0 y (submissionCount == 0 OR política explícita que permita auto-rechazo).
- Pseudocódigo:
  const tasks = db.query("SELECT id, expiryTime,... FROM tasks WHERE expiryTime < NOW() - INTERVAL 'AUTO_REFUND_DAYS' AND phase='awaiting_settlement' AND award_count = 0");
  for (t of tasks) {
    if (policyAllowsAutoRefund(t)) {
      // crear idempotencyKey y encolar una tarea para ejecutar la tx refundExpired con la wallet del servicio
      relayer.relayRefundExpired(t.id, idempotencyKey)
      db.recordAutoRefundAttempt(t.id, idempotencyKey)
    } else {
      db.markForEscalation(t.id)
    }
  }
- Requisitos: el servicio debe tener fondos/gas y una wallet operativa, idempotency handling, auditoría y roll-back o nota en el UI. Consideraciones legales y de disputa: documentar y exponer en UI que el servicio puede ejecutar refund automatizado tras X días.

4) Rehabilitar o proveer fallback de mensajería (XMTP / email)
- El informe muestra que XMTP está deshabilitado en la instalación. Rehabilitar la integración servidor-side o proveer un fallback de notificación por email/SMS. Registrar y validar emails al crear requester accounts para evitar nulls.

5) Investigad y corregid el posible bug de filtrado "phase=awaiting_settlement" que el informante dice que devuelve vacío
- Reproducción recomendada (instrucciones a ops):
  curl -s 'https://api.taskmarket.dev/api/tasks?limit=1&phase=awaiting_settlement' -v
  Revisar logs del handler de /api/tasks para ver si el query param phase está siendo ignorado o si la derivación de phase (expiryTime + status) tiene error o caching.
- Añadir tests de integración que creen una tarea con expiryTime=now-1s y verifiquen que la lista con phase=awaiting_settlement la incluye.

6) Métricas y alertas
- Crear dashboard/alerta: número y valor neto de tareas con phase awaiting_settlement; alerta si crece por encima de small threshold o si alguna tarea está > 7/14/30 días.

Consideraciones de producto y seguridad
- Automáticamente mover o reembolsar contenidos con submissions activas perjudica a trabajadores. Si se va a automatizar reembolso, decidir política clara sobre cómo tratar tareas con envíos activos (requerir rechazo explícito por requester, o permitir auto-reject con logging y posible apelación).
- Implementar auditoría (quién/qué lanzó el refund) y un proceso de apelación.

Pasos concretos que puedo ayudar a ejecutar si me facilitan más recursos
- Redactar un PR sobre el backend (job + worker-visible pendingAction + tests) si me proporcionan el repositorio del backend y las políticas de despliegue.
- Escribir un script de emergencia (operador) para ejecutar manualmente refunds/escalados en producción si el equipo quiere una intervención inmediata.

Conclusión
No he aplicado cambios porque el repositorio actual no contiene el código relevante (solo la documentación/CLI). Resolver #61 exige cambios en el backend, en la lógica de la cola/worker que crea pendingActions y en la infraestructura de notificaciones/relayer. He listado recomendaciones técnicas y operativas con pseudocódigo y pasos de validación; si los mantenedores abren el repositorio del servicio que expone /api/tasks o me dan acceso a él, puedo preparar el PR y las pruebas necesarias.

Resoluble desde este repositorio: no (resolvable=false). Si queréis, indícadme dónde está el backend (repo/URL) o dad acceso a la infraestructura y preparo los cambios y tests para un PR.

opportunities.excerpt:
Posted via Koduo. $25 bounty.

<!-- koduo:solver=ai -->

judgement.reason: Adding a /version HTTP endpoint is a self-contained code change that can be implemented by reading and editing the repository source. It does not require credentials, hardware access, or executing compiled binaries to produce a correct patch. The main unknowns are framework details and how the project exposes its version (constant, package metadata, build-time variable, or git tag). Those are resolvable by inspecting the repo and implementing a reasonable approach (e.g., expose package/version constant or read from a VERSION file). Verification is straightforward by reviewing the change or running existing tests; an agent that cannot run the server can still produce a patch and unit test addition.
plan: Clone the repository and inspect the web server/router code to locate existing HTTP endpoints and the router setup (e.g., main, server, handlers).
Search the repo for an existing version identifier (package.json, setup.cfg, go module version variable, VERSION file, build constants, or git tags). Decide on source of truth for the version.

Add a new handler function for GET /version that returns a small JSON payload such as {"version":"x.y.z"} and appropriate content-type and status code. If the project uses a particular response schema or helper, follow that pattern.

Wire the handler into the router so the endpoint is reachable at /version, respecting any existing middleware (auth, logging) as appropriate. Ensure it is unauthenticated if the intent is public info.
Add or update unit/integration tests: test the handler returns 200 and the expected JSON structure and version string (use a deterministic version source or mock if needed).
Update README or API docs to mention the new /version endpoint and expected response.
Run linter/static checks and update code comments; prepare a single commit with changes and a descriptive commit message, and open a pull request with a short description and test results.

If the repository expects the version to be injected at build time, include documentation in the PR describing how to set the build variable or include a fallback (e.g., 'dev' or contents of VERSION file).

opportunities.title: [Bug]: GR00T-N1.7 eval image preprocessing ignores processor_config (use_albumentations, crop_fraction, letter_box_transform) and diverges from Isaac-GR00T
opportunities.excerpt:
## Your current environment

GB200 (aarch64), vLLM-Omni `10701e18` (main), vLLM 0.28.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.14.1.
Reference: Isaac-GR00T `51d4c89` (torch 2.11.0+cu130, transformers 4.57.6, albumentations 1.4.18, opencv 5.0.0.93).

## Your code version

`10701e18`

## 🐛 Describe the bug

`Gr00tN1d7Processor` (`vllm_omni/diffusion/models/gr00t/modeling/processing_gr00t_n1d7.py`) rebuilds the GR00T-N1.7 eval image transform in torchvision and swallows the checkpoint's `use_albumentations` / `letter_box_transform` keys in `**kwargs`. Both public checkpoints (`nvidia/GR00T-N1.7-3B`, `nvidia/GR00T-N1.7-DROID`) ship

```json
"use_albumentations": true, "letter_box_transform": false, "crop_fraction": 0.95,
"shortest_image_edge": 256, "image_target_size": [256, 256], "image_crop_size": [230, 230]
```

so Isaac-GR00T (what the checkpoints were trained with) and vLLM-Omni preprocess differently:

| step | Isaac-GR00T eval (`use_albumentations=True`) | vLLM-Omni main |
|---|---|---|
| letterbox | only if `letter_box_transform` (False here) | unconditional `LetterBoxTransform()` |
| resize | `SmallestMaxSize(256, INTER_AREA)` | `Resize([256, 256])`, bilinear |
| crop | `Fraction

judgement.reason: The issue is a straightforward mismatch between how processor config keys from checkpoints (use_albumentations, letter_box_transform, crop_fraction, etc.) are handled and how the code currently rebuilds the eval image preprocessing pipeline. An agent that can read the repo can locate the processing implementation, modify the transform builder to honor the processor_config values (and to optionally delegate to albumentations), and add tests. No credentials, binary execution, or hardware access are required; the change is verifiable by static inspection and by running unit tests comparing transform outputs.
plan: Locate the eval preprocessing implementation: open vllm_omni/diffusion/models/gr00t/modeling/processing_gr00t_n1d7.py and identify where the pipeline is built and where **kwargs are swallowed.

Add explicit parsing of processor_config / checkpoint keys: read use_albumentations, letter_box_transform, crop_fraction, shortest_image_edge, image_target_size, image_crop_size from the provided kwargs/processor_config and set sensible fallbacks to existing constants.

When use_albumentations == True: build the evaluation transform pipeline using albumentations primitives that match Isaac-GR00T behavior (conditional LetterBox, SmallestMaxSize with INTER_AREA resizing, fractional/center crop with crop_fraction or provided image_crop_size, final resize to image_target_size). Ensure the pipeline replicates order and interpolation modes used by Isaac-GR00T.

When use_albumentations == False: construct an equivalent torchvision transforms pipeline that mirrors Isaac-GR00T semantics (use torchvision.transforms.functional.resize with INTER_AREA via PIL’s BOX/Resampling method if available or nearest equivalent), conditional letterbox only if letter_box_transform True, and fractional/center crop logic using crop_fraction.

Remove swallowing of **kwargs: ensure remaining kwargs do not drop these keys and that any passed-in processor_config is honored. Add logging or assertions to detect unknown/unused config keys to avoid regressions.

Add unit tests: create tests that load a small sample image and a sample checkpoint-like config (matching public checkpoints) and assert the built pipeline includes/omits LetterBoxTransform appropriately, uses SmallestMaxSize semantics, and produces deterministic output shapes. Add a comparison test that constructs both albumentations and torchvision branches with identical config and verifies shape and approximate pixel statistics are consistent.

Run linters and type checks, update any docstrings/comments describing the preprocessing behavior, and prepare a small PR with the change, test, and a brief rationale referencing Isaac-GR00T behavior and the checkpoint fields.

I have a tested candidate patch for [tscircuit/autorouting#92](https://github.com/tscircuit/autorouting/issues/92), which advertises a $50 bounty. The original repository is archived, so I cannot open a pull request there. I am posting here because the main project directs issue reports to this tracker.

The patch removes the forward-direction rejection based on `node.parent?.obstacleHit`. An obstacle encountered by the parent does not establish that the current forward path is blocked. The existing collision checks from the current point continue to enforce obstacle clearance; backward-direction filtering is unchanged.

The regression uses a minimal intermediate A* state after moving past a wall. The original code returns no forward neighbor despite a clear path to the goal; the patched code reaches the goal. A second test confirms that an actual wall still stops forward travel. A debug SVG snapshot is included. This isolates a logic error consistent with #92; I have not reproduced the original Wi-Fi-board screenshot or established that it resolves every wild jump in that board. This is a patch for the archived implementation, not a claim of a defect in the replacement autorouter.

# Prerequisite
Confirmed this issue has not already been filed. Searched all open and closed issues for `setExpenditureState`, `isValidLocalSkill`, `executeStateChange`, and `skills` bypass -- no prior report found.

## Summary

`ColonyExpenditure.setExpenditureState` validates `_keys[1] <= 3` when writing to `EXPENDITURESLOTS_SLOT` (slot 26) but only requires `_keys.length >= 2`, not exactly 2. When an arbitrator passes `_keys.length == 3` with `_keys[1] == 3` (the `skills` dynamic array field) and `_mask = [MAPPING, ARRAY, ARRAY]`, the `executeStateChange` helper traverses through the array's length slot into its data storage and writes to `skills[0]` directly via `sstore`. This completely bypasses the `isValidLocalSkill()` validation enforced by `setExpenditureSkills`, allowing an arbitrator to attach any valid network skillId -- including the network mining skill -- to an expenditure slot, granting the recipient reputation in an arbitrary skill when the payout is claimed.

## Steps to Reproduce (for bugs)

Two sequential calls by an account holding **Arbitration role** in the expenditure's domain:

**Step 1 -- set `skills` array length to 1** (keys.length = 2, passes existing v
